title: The $50 Million Mistake
story:
In 1997, Netflix started as a DVD rental service. By 2007, it launched its streaming platform.
Today it produces its own content and dominates global streaming.
Blockbuster had the chance to buy Netflix for $50 million in 2000… and declined.

title: Nintendo: A Masterclass in Reinvention
story:
Founded in 1889 in Japan, Nintendo made handmade hanafuda cards.
It experimented with taxis, love hotels, and instant rice before hitting success with electronic toys and consoles.
The name “Nintendo” roughly means “Leave luck to heaven.”

title: Slack: The Accidental Pivot That Changed How We Work
story:
Glitch failed in 2012, but the team realized their internal communication tool was valuable. That tool became Slack.
Slack stands for “Searchable Log of All Conversation and Knowledge.”

title: YouTube: From Video Dating to Viral Zoo Clip
story:
It launched on Valentine’s Day 2005 as a video dating site: “Tune In, Hook Up.”
Users started uploading all kinds of videos, not just dating intros.
Fun fact:
The first video ever uploaded was “Me at the zoo,” by co-founder Jawed Karim.

title: Twitter: The $5 Million Pivot from Odeo
story:
When Apple announced iTunes would support podcasts, Odeo knew it was doomed.
Employees were encouraged to brainstorm new ideas. Jack Dorsey pitched Twitter.
The original name for Twitter was “Twttr,” inspired by Flickr and SMS’s 140-character limit.

title: Shopify: Built from Snowboards into a Global Powerhouse
story:
The founders wanted to sell snowboards online but found existing e-commerce tools terrible.
They built their own — and realized it was a business opportunity.
Shopify powers over 4 million businesses today, including major brands like Allbirds and Gymshark.

title: Instagram: The Power of Pivoting from Burbn
story:
Burbn had too many features — check-ins, photos, gaming elements.
Founders noticed users mostly used it to share photos. They stripped everything else and launched Instagram.
Instagram gained 25,000 users in one day after launching in 2010.

title: PayPal: How a PalmPilot Security Tool Became a Global Payment Powerhouse
story:
It began as Confinity, building cryptography software for handheld devices.
They pivoted to enabling money transfers via email — which became PayPal.
Elon Musk merged his online banking startup, X.com, with Confinity to form PayPal.

title: Wrigley: From Soap to Gum Empire
story:
William Wrigley Jr. gave away gum as a promotional item.
The gum became more popular than the soap or baking powder.
The company created iconic gum brands like Juicy Fruit and Doublemint.

title: Nokia: From Paper Mill to Telecom Titan
story:
Founded in 1865 in Finland as a pulp mill. Later made tires and rubber boots.
Became a telecom giant, then faded out in smartphones, and now focuses on network equipment.
The classic Nokia 3310 is legendary for its durability — and "Snake" game.

title: Airbnb: From Air Mattresses to Obama O’s to Global Disruption
story: Started as “AirBed & Breakfast” to provide lodging during conferences. To fund their startup, the founders sold cereal boxes labeled “Obama O’s” and “Cap’n McCain’s” during the 2008 U.S. election.

title: Pinterest: Pivoting from Tote to Visual Discovery
story: Originally a shopping app, the founders noticed users were more interested in collecting and sharing images of products than purchasing them, leading to the creation of Pinterest.

title: Play‑Doh: From Wallpaper Cleaner to Toy Icon
story: Initially used to clean soot from wallpaper, Play-Doh was repurposed as a children's toy when demand for wallpaper cleaner declined post-World War II.

title: Suzuki: From Silk Looms to Global Mobility Titan
story: Founded as a loom manufacturer for Japan's silk industry, Suzuki diversified into motor vehicles after World War II due to declining demand for looms.

title: Avon: From Books to Beauty Empires
story: Avon began by selling books door-to-door, offering perfume samples as incentives. The perfumes became more popular than the books, prompting a pivot to cosmetics.

title: Western Union: From Telegraphs to Global Money Transfers
story: Originally a telegraph company, Western Union shifted focus to financial services as telegraphy became obsolete, capitalizing on its existing infrastructure for money transfers.

title: Flickr: From Game Feature to Photo-Sharing Platform
story: Developed as a feature within an online game, Flickr's photo-sharing tool gained popularity, leading the company to focus solely on photo sharing.

title: HP: From Garage-Built Oscillators to Global Tech Leader
story: Started in a garage producing electronic test equipment, HP expanded into computing and became a leading PC and printer manufacturer.

title: Fab.com: From Gay Social Network to Design E-Commerce Powerhouse
story: Initially a social network, Fab.com pivoted to flash sales of design products, achieving rapid growth before eventually declining.

title: Marriott: From Root Beer Stand to Global Hospitality Leader
story: Marriott began as a root beer stand in Washington, D.C., expanded into restaurants, and eventually opened its first hotel in 1957, growing into a global hospitality company.
